answer.label: In short
answer.lead: A marketing guide is a plain explanation of one decision, with the method and a worked example, so you can apply it to your own numbers. MMC writes guides on the decisions that decide whether marketing makes money, for D2C founders and marketers, each linked to a free calculator or service. They use made-up examples and promise no results.

leaks.lede: Each guide starts from a mistake we see often. Pick the one closest to yours.

stages.breaks: Judging campaigns on the ROAS a dashboard shows.
stages.why: Product cost, shipping, fees and returns decide what an order leaves behind, and so the ROAS you need.
stages.does: The guide shows how to work out your break-even ROAS from your own costs, with a worked example.

stages.breaks: Adding up what each platform reports.
stages.why: Each platform claims the sales it can link to itself, so the totals often exceed your real orders.
stages.does: The guide shows how to start from store orders, track blended ROAS and check the big decisions with simple tests.

stages.breaks: Making ads on instinct and keeping the loudest.
stages.why: Without controlled tests, you cannot say why an ad worked, so you cannot repeat it.
stages.does: The guide shows how to test hooks, angles and formats, read the results and refresh before ads tire.

cards.d: Break-even ROAS, unit economics, LTV:CAC, runway, funnel and growth calculators.
